result.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection
result.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
result.summary: Face presentation attack detection requires representations that distinguish physical spoofing cues across changes in acquisition devices, subjects, and attack media. Large visual encoders offer transferable representations, but conventional binary fine-tuning supervises their final decisions without explicitly constraining how local facial evidence is represented under partial observation. We present CP-JEPA, a context-predictive adaptation framework that combines low-rank tuning of a pretrained CLIP image encoder with a joint-embedding predictive objective. A student predicts complete-image teacher features at masked spatial locations, while unmasked classification, masked classification, and prediction consistency retain the connection to the live/spoof task. An exponential-moving-average teacher supplies evolving latent targets. The auxiliary components are used only during training; inference requires only the LoRA-adapted CLIP visual encoder and binary classifier. {We evaluate CP-JEPA under single-source and multi-source OCIM transfer, additional CelebA-Spoof training, transfer to CelebA-Spoof, two-source training, and unseen-attack evaluation on SiW-Mv2.} On the standard OCIM benchmark, CP-JEPA achieves 3.74\% mean HTER and 98.73\% mean AUC. {Single-source evaluation achieves 11.36\% mean HTER across twelve source--target combinations.} With CelebA-Spoof added to the three OCIM training sources, CP-JEPA reduces mean HTER from 3.45\% to 2.35\% and increases mean AUC from 98.68\% to 99.32\%. On SiW-Mv2, it achieves 3.36\% mean HTER across the held-out attack categories. Controlled loss ablations examine the contributions of latent prediction, masked classification, and prediction consistency. The results show that context-predictive adaptation can improve cross-dataset PAD performance, although the gains vary with the training sources and evaluation setting.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 CP-JEPA，用 LoRA 微调 CLIP 图像编码器，并在训练期加入掩码空间位置的联合嵌入预测目标（学生预测完整图像教师特征，配合 EMA 教师以及未掩码/掩码分类与预测一致性），用于人脸活体攻击检测的跨数据集迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 掩码位置的 latent 特征预测与 EMA 目标可视为训练期对内部视觉状态的约束线索，可能为 LVR 中部分观测下视觉细节保留与 latent 监督提供参考；但该工作是 PAD 分类，推理期无 latent 推理或答案使用，联系需进一步核查。
